subject: Zero Inflated Poisson in the pcount model

messages.author: c52d6613363308cd
messages.subject: Zero Inflated Poisson in the pcount model
parts:
I would like to confirm my understanding of a few items related to the
behavior of the pcount model when using the zero inflated poisson
error structure.

1) I am assuming that the parameter called psi is the probability of a
site NOT having a non-zero abundance at a particular site. My
confusion is because this is the converse of the meaning of psi
typically used in occupancy type models where psi is the site
occupancy probability or the proportion of occupied sites. The help
file states "the mean is lambda*(1-psi)" so I believe I am correct but
would like confirmation.

2) I am fitting the model with a categorical site covariate (Bottom is
hard, mixed, or soft). It appears that the ZIP is parameterized is to
have a shared psi value for each covariate level. Is that correct?

Many thanks,

Lew

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Zero Inflated Poisson in the pcount model
parts:
hi Lew,
 (1) Not exactly.   psi is the probability that N is a realization from a Poisson distribution -- so you could still get N=0 in that case.    1-psi is the probability that N is a fixed zero.  
 It is true that the marginal expectation of N is lambda*(1-psi).

 (2) I think this is correct -- you would always have the same zero-inflation probability but this leads to different marginal probabilities that N = 0 if you let lambda vary. so there is some flexibility there (i.e., if psi varies by substrate but not lambda, but the model says lambda varies but not psi, then you might get almost equivalent fits)

regards
andy
